title: Can you override private and static methods?
shortTitle: Can you override private and static methods?
keyPoints: private methods CANNOT be overridden – they are not visible to subclasses at all
static methods CANNOT be overridden – they are hidden, not overridden (resolved by reference type at compile time)
A subclass can define a method with the same name as a private parent method – but it is a completely new method, not an override
A subclass can define a static method with the same signature – this is method hiding, not overriding
@Override on a private-named method compiles (it is a new method), but @Override on a static method does not compile

s1_definition.oneliner: No. Private methods are invisible to subclasses. Static methods are hidden, not overridden. Neither participates in runtime polymorphism.
s1_definition.profdef:
Two types that cannot be overridden:

- **private:** Not visible outside the class. A subclass that defines the same-named method is creating a new, independent method. It has no relationship to the parent's private method.
- **static:** Belongs to the class, not to objects. A subclass can define the same static signature, but this is hiding (compile-time resolution by reference type), not overriding (runtime resolution by object type).
s1_definition.analogy: A bank's private internal audit procedure (private method) is invisible to branch offices. A branch can create its own audit procedure with the same name, but it has no connection to the head office's procedure. A bank notice posted on a specific wall (static method) can be covered by a branch's own notice (hiding), but the head office's notice is still there underneath – looking from the head office reference, you see the original.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Overridable:       public/protected instance methods → runtime dispatch
  NOT overridable:   private  → invisible to subclass (new method, not override)
                     static   → hidden, not overridden (compile-time dispatch)
                     final    → compiler rejects any attempt

  Account a = new SavingsAccount();
    a.process()        → calls Account.audit() (private, not overridden)
    a.getType()        → calls Bank.getType() (static, not overridden)
    a.calculateRate()  → calls SavingsAccount.calculateRate() (overridden!)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Private methods cannot be overridden because they are invisible to subclasses. A subclass can define a method with the same name, but it is a completely new, independent method with no relationship to the parent's private method.

Static methods cannot be overridden because they belong to the class, not to objects. A subclass can define the same static signature, but this is method hiding: the call is resolved by the reference type at compile time, not by the object type at runtime.

Only public and protected instance methods participate in overriding and runtime polymorphism.

One sentence to remember: private is invisible so it cannot be overridden, static is resolved at compile time so it can only be hidden – neither participates in polymorphism.
